intro.text: Less common third moves for Black. Each has a clear idea, and knowing the best reply gives White an easy, comfortable game.
The Ruy Lopez: White develops the bishop to attack the knight that protects Black's centre pawn. Its pressure is slow but lasting, and it has been a main opening at every level for centuries.
Black develops the king's knight to a modest square to avoid pins and keep the f-pawn flexible.
Black prepares to develop the dark-squared bishop on the long diagonal, a hypermodern setup that lets White build a big centre.
Black offers a knight trade at once. It costs time, and White usually gets a comfortable lead in development.
Against the Cozio setup White develops naturally and keeps central options. Black usually reroutes the knight to the kingside.

white.text: White's winners used the knight jump Nd5 to exploit Black's slow development.
